proposals.premise: Visitors primarily need quick reassurance, opening times and a clear choice between the main and step-free entrances.
proposals.opening: Desktop shows arrival guidance beside the entry photograph; phone shows “You can just arrive” first, followed by doors 09:00–17:00, quiet hour 13:00–14:00 and the same photograph.
proposals.move: The first control, “Choose your way in,” switches between five-step main entrance and step-free library-courtyard directions; the selected route appears directly below.
proposals.tradeoff: This makes independent arrival fastest, but volunteer help is less prominent.

proposals.premise: Assume visitors may not know the courtyard entrance by name; the real photograph can anchor recognition before they decide whether they need help.
proposals.opening: Desktop pairs the door, bells and curb photograph with step-free instructions and volunteer help; phone leads with the photograph, then identifies the courtyard bell, indoor chairs and entrance conditions.
proposals.move: The first control, “Request a courtyard welcome,” opens an arrival-time picker restricted to times at least 30 minutes ahead; the chosen time appears in a pending request summary.
proposals.tradeoff: Recognition and assisted arrival improve, but independent visitors must read farther to confirm no booking is required.
